checks: For a full-dimensional convex body, Fubini gives the slice-volume density and Brunn–Minkowski gives concavity of the k-th root. At zero-volume fibers the same inequality follows by retaining a point and a homothetic copy of the positive fiber, or is trivial if both are zero.

Closedness in a common bounded box and reverse Fatou give upper semicontinuity of canonical slice volume. Every interior projection point lifts to an interior point by mixing an interior lift with a lift farther along the projected line, giving full support.

Equal measures give equal projections and equal continuous interior densities. Along a segment from an interior point to a boundary point, concavity gives the required lower limit and upper semicontinuity the reverse, identifying the canonical boundary values as well.

For m≥2, the other concave root would equal a positive constant times R^{m/(m-1)}, strictly convex on the nonconstant positive affine segment. For m=1 the zero-perpendicular-dimensional alternative has density one on its own projected convex body, also at boundary in its canonical version.
Original 2961bff576f5c43e §3 gives this exponent obstruction. The frozen proof closes the a.e.-to-canonical issue for segments in the boundary.

dependencies.hypotheses: Apply the k-dimensional volume-root inequality to nonempty compact slice sets and their Minkowski inclusion; the elementary zero-volume cases are also covered directly.
dependencies.reference: Brunn–Minkowski inequality, Gardner, The Brunn–Minkowski inequality, (2) and (10)

overlap.comparison: Contains the concavity and upper semicontinuity ingredients for the old marginal but preserves the original perpendicular dimension. It does not prove this dimension-deletion obstruction for arbitrary Borel equality.

Concerns intrinsic one-dimensional lengths of two null ambient fibers under partial Schwarz symmetry. The present claim is about a full-dimensional real projected volume measure and compares two slice dimensions.

readability: The canonical boundary argument is needed because a segment may be entirely null for ambient projected Lebesgue measure.
review_method: Independent cold proof read, exact arithmetic where applicable, and pinned source/dependency comparison
summary: The slice-root obstruction applies to equality of Borel marginals, including an affine-radius segment on the projection boundary.
